subject: English
passage: Our violin instructor, Katherine Morgan, brought her younger sister, Sophia, to my lesson one day. By now I was seventeen and had mastered everything Katherine had to teach me, so I welcomed a new presence. Sophia was an aspiring composer, and she had heard from her sister that I was none other than the daughter of James Cole, and I was a musical prodigy. Sophia was hoping not only to meet me but to have the chance to meet the renowned pianist himself at our home.
prompt: Based on the text, why does Sophia accompany her sister to the narrator's house one day?

choices.A: Sophia has mastered all her sister can teach her and now desires to be taught by the narrator.
choices.B: Sophia has not received formal instruction in composition and wants to ask the narrator's famous father to be her mentor.
choices.C: Sophia wants to perform her compositions for the narrator and receive feedback on her work.
choices.D: Sophia anticipates having the opportunity to be introduced to both the narrator and her father.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it captures both elements of Sophia's dual motivation as explicitly stated in the text. The passage uses 'not only...but' to indicate Sophia has two goals: 'Sophia was hoping not only to meet me but to have the chance to meet the renowned pianist himself at our home.' Choice D paraphrases this complete motivation, using 'anticipates having the opportunity to be introduced to both the narrator and her father'—corresponding to 'me' and 'the renowned pianist himself.' By synthesizing these two textual elements, Choice D provides the most accurate answer to why Sophia accompanies her sister.
